concepts.def: Vast gravitationally bound system of stars, gas and dust.
Disc-shaped galaxy with curved arms, like the Milky Way.
Round/oval galaxy of mostly older stars and little gas.
Galaxy with no clear shape, often small and gas-rich.
Our spiral galaxy, about 100,000 light-years across.
Cluster of ~80 galaxies including Milky Way and Andromeda.

walkthroughs.body_html: Spirals have arms of young blue stars; ellipticals are smooth balls of older red stars; irregulars lack clear structure and are often star-forming.
The Milky Way is a barred spiral about 100,000 light-years across, containing roughly 100 billion stars. The Sun lies about 26,000 light-years from its centre.
Andromeda (M31) is the largest galaxy in the Local Group, about 2.5 million light-years away. It is approaching the Milky Way and will merge with it in about 4-5 billion years.
